subject: NovaCorp — usage buckets & context sizing (pricing recap and next steps)
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@novacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: NovaCorp discovery — context sizing + token buckets (recap)

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Below is a short recap of the things we discussed and a sizing ask so we can put an initial pricing sketch together. Aim is to land a target $/1M token that fits your budget range and reflect the split across short/long context calls.

Call highlights (quick):
- Use case: AI-powered customer support summarization + on-demand knowledge retrieval for enterprise customers (mix of short and long contexts).
- Traffic profile: product team expects high traffic during weekday hours, peaks aligned with support SLAs.
- Data residency: US-only for now.

Sizing inputs I asked for (if you can confirm or attach a sample extract):
1) Monthly active requests and average prompt/completion sizes per workload bucket (we discussed three buckets: short, medium, long).
2) % of requests that require 8k vs 32k vs 128k context (estimate fine).
3) Any hard budget band — you mentioned a rough target per-month spend range; want the exact band to tune the unit economics.

What I captured from today (please correct):
- Monthly request volume: ~2.5M total LLM calls (mix of summaries + retrieval-augmented generation).
- Distribution guess: Short (<=512 prompt / <=512 completion): 50% of calls; Medium (512–4k prompt / ~1k completion): 35% of calls; Long (>4k prompt or chain of docs, needs 32k/128k): 15% of calls.
- Average tokens (ballpark): short: prompt 220 / completion 480; medium: prompt 1,400 / completion 900; long: prompt 9,000 / completion 1,800 (these numbers are my workback — please provide your measured averages when available).
- Budget guidance you mentioned: target $/1M tokens in the neighborhood of $1,500 — $4,000 depending on context length and SLA.

Next steps (our side):
- If you can share a small sample CSV of average prompt/completion lengths by endpoint, we will produce: (a) projected monthly token volumes by bucket, (b) three price scenarios (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and (c) latency/cost tradeoffs for enabling 8k/32k/128k.
- I'll loop Ben (procurement lead) if you want help with procurement calendar and rough SOW.

Attachments: I attached a one-pager request template and a blank CSV for your export.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Confirmed numbers (from our telemetry export):
- Monthly LLM calls: 2,750,000
- Short (support quick replies): 52% — average prompt 195 tokens / avg completion 420 tokens
- Medium (2–4 doc blends): 33% — avg prompt 1,350 tokens / avg completion 1,050 tokens
- Long (policy/legal batch reads, occasionally >100k chars): 15% — distribution between heavy 32k needs (10%) and very-long 128k experiments (5%). For the long bucket, median prompt is ~8,400 tokens, median completion 1,600 tokens.

Budget: procurement asked us to target an initial unit-price target of $2,200 / 1M tokens (total tokens consumed) but we have flexibility to go up to $3,800 if latency SLOs are strict and private deployment is required.

I'm attaching a 2-week sample of anonymized token-lengths by endpoint — should help you bake realistic mixes.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up Friday to review your draft estimate.

— Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: NovaCorp discovery — context sizing + token buckets (recap)

Alex — perfect, thanks for the CSV. I ran a quick back-of-envelope and here are two pricing sketches to align on before Friday:

Assumptions used (from your telemetry + conservative headroom):
- Monthly total tokens consumed = sum(prompt + completion) across calls. Using your medians gives ~3.1B tokens/month.
- Split by context: short 52% (avg 615 tokens per call), medium 33% (avg 2,400 tokens per call), long 15% (avg 10,000 tokens per call).
- Performance targets: p95 latency <300ms for short calls; <800ms for medium; <2s for long (with asynchronous options).

Scenario A — Hosted (fastest onboarding):
- Suggested blended unit rate: $2,600 / 1M tokens
- Monthly cost estimate: ~$8,060 (wait, recalculation)

Oops — mis-typed the projection in-line. Let me be explicit: with 3.1B tokens/month, at $2,600 / 1M tokens => monthly = (3,100 * $2,600) = $8,060,000.

Scenario B — Dedicated (reserved capacity + better unit economics):
- Discounted blended unit rate: $1,750 / 1M tokens with a 12-month commit and predictable traffic shaping
- Monthly cost estimate: (3,100 * $1,750) = $5,425,000

Operational levers we recommend to reduce the blended $/1M:
- Prefix & KV caching for the short bucket — can cut short bucket token usage by ~30–45% depending on prompt reuse.
- Aggressive truncation+structured prompts for short replies to push average completion down from 420 -> ~300 tokens.
- For long workloads, use chunked retrieval + reranking to avoid always passing full 128k contexts; this can reduce average prompt tokens by ~25–40%.
- Consider a hybrid: host short+medium requests on Redwood Hosted, and route long/128k experiments to Dedicated or Private nodes with specialized kernels (better $/token for large contexts).

Action items before Friday call:
1) We'll produce a detailed spreadsheet with token-by-endpoint breakouts + three price runs (hosted/dedicated/private).
2) Ben, can you take point on procurement steps and a draft T&Cs outline?
3) Alex — please confirm whether the 128k use is experimental (spikes) or expected to be steady-state. If experimental, we can recommend burst routing.

I'll attach the initial pricing PDF in an hour.

Thanks —
Karthik

2) Term: we prefer 12 months to retain flexibility, willing to pilot with 12 months and re-evaluate.
3) Budget guardrail: we can commit to a target blended $/1M tokens of $1,900 if Redwood can guarantee routing/fallbacks that keep p95 latency for short calls under 350ms.

Alex
